subject: detail on gl.filter.monomorphs: Remove monomorphic loci

messages.author: b09b3731856b6d56
messages.subject: detail on gl.filter.monomorphs: Remove monomorphic loci
parts: Dear Arthur, I would like to know how the function gl.filter.monomorphs works. I understood (but perhaps I am wrong), this function removes the monomorphic loci by taking into account all the loci without paying attention to the populations. What seems to me well, particularly in the case where the monomorphy brings a signature of differentiation to the population compared to the others. Are there some thresholds to decide the monomorphy? Could we set this threshold in this function? Many thanks for your help, Have a wonderful end of day, Natacha

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: detail on gl.filter.monomorphs: Remove monomorphic loci
parts:
Hi Nat,

The filter gl.filter.monomorphs is typically used to take out monomorphic loci arising when you manipulate the DArT dataset by deleting individuals or populations. The original DArT dataset should not have any monomorphic loci because the pipelines select for polymorphic loci, those containing SNPs.

The filter is also used to take out monomophic loci where these will not contribute materially to analyses, to save computational time or prevent distortion of outcomes. By default, dartR scripts retain monomophic loci. You have to explicitly request that the be removed by setting mono.rm=TRUE in the particular script, or by using gl.filter.monomorphs. Most scripts will warn you if the dataset contains monomorphic loci.

If you want to manipulate loci that are almost monomorphic, then you should use the filter for minor allele fequencies, gl.filter.maf, which has the threshold you have requested. Please look at ?gl.filter.maf.

Hope this helps.

Arthur
